Proposition
[Metric induced by a length space] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0412 ↗ def:chow-iii-quasi-length-space 1. appG:G.6\group Length spaces

The associated distance $d_{\cL }$ of a quasi-length space is a quasi-metric. For a length space it is a metric (possibly taking the value $\infty $); a metric obtained this way is called intrinsic, and it is strictly intrinsic when the length structure is complete.
Proof

\sketch Concatenating paths through an intermediate point proves the triangle inequality. The length-space topology and nonnegativity give finiteness, symmetry, and separation in the metric case.

□
